card_quote: Buys the gift, not the book; judges by the cover, the back blurb and whether it looks like it is for him. Wants something he can pick up for two minutes.
how_read: Flips through it at the kitchen table before wrapping it. Reads the dedication page and the how-to-play page, then works through the first round to see if Dave would actually sit with it. Skims a few more pages, decides it is giftable, and wraps it. Does not read it cover to cover.

w1_friction.note: A whole page of rules before the fun starts. Dave will not read this, he will just flip to a question.
w1_friction.quote: Decide before turning over: TRUE, FOLKLORE or DISPUTED

w1_friction.note: The answer is a full page of small print. That is not a two-minute pick-up, that is homework.
w1_friction.quote: The popular version is a single moment.

w1_friction.note: Wait, the last page said the apple thing was folklore and now it is TRUE? I had to read it twice.
w1_friction.quote: Newton told of an apple; nobody needed to invent it

w1_friction.note: Lost me at the formula. I did science in 1983.
DISPUTED feels like a cop-out. If you are a quiz book, give me an answer.
w1_friction.quote: Who first said it, and in what words, is not settled.

w1_friction.note: Everybody says blood, sweat and tears. Calling that folklore over one extra word feels picky.
w1_friction.quote: That is four items, not three

w1_best.why: Everyone knows the apple on the head. Fun to hear it is not quite so.
The bath and Eureka, I thought that was gospel. Good one to read to him at dinner.
Never knew Einstein's prize was not for relativity. That is a good party fact.
I have quoted that line my whole life. Now I know about the toil.
Galileo and the tower was a school story. Short enough that I finished it.

w1_flat.why: A formula and a lot of names. Dave would put it down.
Chips and 18 months, no picture in my head, not a story.
Confusing after the apple one, felt like the same question again.
Babylonian tablets and triples. School math, not a dinner fact.
A lot of words to end on disputed.

w1_review.headline: Looks like a good stocking gift, reads a bit like homework
w1_review.body: The cover and the idea are clever and the guess-then-turn-the-page thing is a nice way to get a non-reader to try one. But the answer pages are a lot of small print for a man who gives a book two minutes at a time. I would give it as a gift if the price is right, and I would not expect him to read all of it. Bottom line: nice present, thin on easy fun.

w2_review_first: It is a quiz book where you guess if famous stories are true. It is a fun idea and it looks good for someone who likes trivia, but I would say the answers go on a bit. I would give it to a person who likes facts, not to my husband to read cover to cover.

w2_lost.why: The first answer was already so long I thought, this is going to be like this all through.
The Einstein formula page, I just skipped to the bottom line.
Murphy's law disputed, a page of back and forth with no answer.

w2_read_aloud.why: Everyone has heard of the bath and Eureka, a good opener.
The apple on the head, you can ask the whole table.
Streisand's house, I remember that being in the news, would be fun.
Rat tails in Hanoi sounds funny and strange, people would lean in.
Buttered toast, everyone has dropped toast, easy to laugh at.

w2_cut.why: Fermat and a margin, I do not even know what that is about.
Prime number theorem sounds like a math class.
Pareto and Italian land, nobody at my table cares.
Uncertainty principle, too hard to read out loud.
Thucydides trap, sounds like a lecture.

w2_book2: If it is the same format with just as much small print on every answer page and the price creeps up.
